milestones.name: Prepare the presentation browser

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: What is ready
actions.body: The native-browser demo is implemented at http://localhost:4200. Install dependencies once with pnpm --dir examples/01-native-browser-models install --frozen-lockfile, then run pnpm --dir examples/01-native-browser-models start from the repository root. The four Angular units are Chat, Summarization, Proofreading, and Translation (German/Spanish). Select a capability, inspect browser-reported availability, explicitly prepare/download, then try the example. Automated state tests pass; real model downloads and inference still require rehearsal on the workshop browser.

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Start this desk
actions.body: From hands-on-local-llms, run the command below. Open http://localhost:4412. Node 24 is available on this machine; no package installation or API key is required.

actions.label: PREPARE
actions.title: Use desktop Chrome
actions.body: Use an eligible Chrome desktop profile and a secure top-level page (HTTPS or localhost). Confirm the actual version and API exposure. The core web Prompt API is documented as stable from Chrome 148; extension support starts at 138. Web sampling controls remain a separate experimental feature.

actions.label: PREPARE
actions.title: Check hardware and storage
actions.body: For Nano-backed APIs, Chrome documents 22 GB free storage, and either more than 4 GB VRAM or a CPU with at least 16 GB RAM and four cores. These are eligibility requirements, not the model file size. Use an unmetered connection for preparation. Translator and Language Detector have separate requirements.

actions.label: PREPARE
actions.title: Check experimental proofreading
actions.body: The Proofreader documentation currently describes a developer trial and the localhost flag chrome://flags/#proofreader-api. Its origin-trial dates are historical; do not assume an old trial token remains valid. Rehearse this API explicitly. Do not change browser flags automatically.

milestones.name: Which model does Chrome use?

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: The browser owns model selection
actions.body: Prompt API uses Gemini Nano. Chrome selects a suitable variant for the device. Task APIs may use additional adaptation weights; translation and language detection use specialist models. These API names are capabilities, not a catalogue of user-selectable checkpoints.

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Inspect the installed model
actions.body: Manually open chrome://on-device-internals. Show the installed-model information available in this Chrome build. Ordinary website JavaScript cannot query the exact Nano model version.

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: Connect this to the next chapter
actions.body: Native browser AI supplies the model and its lifecycle. Choosing an application-supplied checkpoint belongs in the following ONNX chapter.

milestones.name: Persistence, repeat visits and offline use

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: Separate three lifetimes
actions.body: Downloaded model resources persist under Chrome’s management. A JavaScript session is a runtime object. Conversation history belongs to that session unless the app separately saves and restores it. Resetting a conversation is not uninstalling a model.

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Repeat without a new model download
actions.body: Prepare while online. Reload the demo at the same origin and profile, inspect availability, create a fresh session and send a new prompt. Expected: reuse of installed resources, subject to updates or eviction. Never equate create() with a mandatory new download.

actions.label: DO
actions.title: Test offline inference
actions.body: Once preparation succeeds, use an offline environment verified to affect model-network access. A page-only DevTools offline switch is not sufficient proof that browser-component downloads are blocked. Send a fresh prompt, not a previously recorded response. This desk does not change network settings.

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: Keep app loading separate
actions.body: An already open page can run inference without downloading its JavaScript again. Reloading a hosted app offline needs app-shell caching. Native model storage is not the website’s Cache Storage or IndexedDB, and storage.persist() does not pin Chrome’s model.

actions.label: EXPLAIN
actions.title: Explain updates and eviction
actions.body: Chrome can update model resources or remove them under storage pressure, policy changes or loss of eligibility. Recheck readiness on later visits. Do not promise permanent retention or download exactly once forever.

actions.label: PREPARE
actions.title: Keep a cold-start fallback
actions.body: Rehearse on the actual presentation profile. If a cold-download demonstration is needed, capture a real first-use session in a separate eligible test profile before the workshop. Record observed behavior rather than assuming it must download.

files.purpose: Show that destroying a session releases its runtime resources.

actions.body: UMAP projects the vectors to 2D. Screen distances are approximate; cosine scores and nearest neighbours use the full vectors.
